1469	## Cut, restore and reset (`upstream.go`, `restore.go`, `reset.go`, `repoapi.go`, DEVDESK-534, NX-02b)
1470	
1471	Three commands, three mise tasks (`nexus-bench:cut-upstream`, `nexus-bench:restore-upstream`,
1472	`nexus-bench:reset`). Each runs a preflight (`OpCut`, `OpRestore`, `OpReset`, see "Errors,
1473	runner and preflight"); `reset` runs its own, as `down` does, the two others get theirs from
1474	the command. None of them can be run on a custom upstream (`NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL`): the
1475	bench scales and empties only the upstream it deploys.
1476	
1477	**`cut-upstream`** (`CutUpstream`). Reads the upstream, scales it to zero replicas when it is
1478	not already cut (one write, never retried), then waits, until `Params.Timeout`, for no pod of
1479	it to be left, a terminating one included (its volume is still mounted). Idempotent. It
1480	touches neither Nexus nor the descriptor and needs no skopeo, no store and no REST host.
1481	Measured: about 2.5 s.
1482	
1483	**`restore-upstream`** (`RestoreUpstream`). Order: the stored credentials are read first (before
1484	any write); `EnsureUpstream` (one replica, wait for ready); `UnblockProxy`; a check, through a
1485	port-forward and with no credential, that each upstream image has the digest of the data set;
1486	a read of each `PullThrough` image through `docker-proxy` as `bench-pull`, digest equal.
1487	It writes no descriptor and copies no image. `UnblockProxy` reads `docker-proxy` (absent is an
1488	error: `up` creates it), sends again the configuration `Provision` writes (`repositorySpecs`,
1489	never one read back from the instance), which lifts the automatic block, then `POST
1490	/v1/repositories/docker-proxy/invalidate-cache`. Measured: 3 to 7 s with the wait for ready.
1491	
1492	**`reset`** (`Reset`). Order: preflight `OpReset`; custom upstream refused; loopback origin
1493	checked; stored credentials, checked by one admin `GET` (a refused password stops everything
1494	before the first deletion); label of the upstream claim checked; `DELETE` of `docker-group`,
1495	`docker-proxy` and `docker-hosted` (a 404 is already done); replacement of the upstream
1496	storage (below); `Provision`; a wait of 30 s at most (`seedListWait`) for `docker-hosted` and
1497	`docker-proxy` to list nothing; `Seed`. The command reads the previous descriptor before
1498	anything and writes it again after a success, with the previous hosts (a reset reads no node);
1499	the file is the same byte for byte. Measured: about 9 to 11 s. `reset` never changes the admin
1500	password (`Provision` gets an `InitialPassword` that never reads the pod) and never rolls or
1501	restarts the Nexus pod; `nexus-data`, the namespace and the passwords are kept.
1502	
1503	**Storage of the upstream** (`recycleUpstreamStorage`). `CutUpstream`; the claim
1504	`bench-upstream-data` is read and its label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench`
1505	checked (D-P: a claim the bench did not create is never deleted); it is deleted with
1506	`kubectl delete --raw /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/persistentvolumeclaims/bench-upstream-data -f -`,
1507	whose body is a `DeleteOptions` with `preconditions.uid` set to the UID just read. `kubectl
1508	delete pvc --wait=false` was not chosen because it has no precondition: a claim replaced since
1509	the read would be deleted. A claim read without a UID is refused. The delete is sent once; the
1510	wait for `NotFound` lasts until `Params.DeleteTimeout`; then the claim alone (document 5 of
1511	`Render`, `renderUpstreamClaim`, never the whole stream, which would roll the Nexus pod) is
1512	applied again and `EnsureUpstream` runs. A claim already gone is not deleted again, and one
1513	still `Terminating` is waited for.
1514	
1515	> **Warning.** Never put `dryRun` in the query of the raw path (`...?dryRun=All`):
1516	> `kubectl delete --raw` does not honor it and the claim is really deleted (seen on the
1517	> bench, DEVDESK-534 step 9). There is no dry run for this call; check with `get pvc`.
1518	
1519	**Half-way.** An error after the first deletion keeps its kind and cause and ends its check
1520	with "the reset stopped half-way: run `mise run nexus-bench:reset` again, it starts over".
1521	What was deleted stays deleted; the reset is idempotent. The one exception is the
1522	repositories that never empty (`errRepositoriesNeverEmpty`): running again would wait for the
1523	same thing, so the check points at the log of the Nexus pod. A cancelled command prints that
1524	the data set may be half deleted.
1525	
1526	**Rights.** `cut`: get `deployments`, list `pods`, patch `deployments/scale`. `restore`: the
1527	list of `seed`. `reset`: that list, plus delete, create and patch `persistentvolumeclaims`;
1528	never `pods/exec`.
1529	
1530	**Loopback guard.** `restore-upstream` and `reset` send the admin credentials in clear text
1531	and go through the port-forwards of this machine, so `--rest-host` must be `127.0.0.1` or
1532	`::1` (`IsLoopbackRESTHost`, the one predicate of the command and the library). `localhost`,
1533	another loopback address (`127.0.0.2`, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`) and any name are refused;
1534	`requireLoopbackBase` also refuses an origin with user information and parses the host, so
1535	`127.0.0.1@evil.example` fails. The port-forward address is checked too
1536	(`checkLoopbackForward`, shared with the seed).
1537	
1538	**Closed lists.** `benchRepositories` (`docker-group`, `docker-proxy`, `docker-hosted`) are the
1539	only repositories `deleteRepository` accepts; `invalidatableRepositories` (`docker-proxy`,
1540	`docker-group`; a hosted repository has no cache) the only ones `invalidateCache` accepts. A
1541	name outside a list is refused before any request, so a name never decides the path the admin
1542	credentials go to.
1543	
1544	**`up` with a cut upstream (D-Q).** `up` reads the upstream before bringing it back; if it was
1545	cut, it calls `UnblockProxy` after `Provision`, so a second `up` leaves the bench nominal. With a
1546	cut upstream and a `--rest-host` that is not loopback, `up` stops before scaling anything (a
1547	refusal later would leave the proxy blocked, since a second `up` finds the upstream ready). If
1548	the unblock itself fails, the error says to run `restore-upstream`.
1549	
1550	**What to know when using it.**
1551	
1552	- After `reset` the Nexus blobs of the deleted repositories are not compacted: `nexus-data`
1553	  grows with each reset. How to get that space back is not measured.
1554	- The admin and `bench-pull` credentials go to the NodePort on the loopback and the images
1555	  through it: this assumes this machine is the node (as before NX-02b; not new).
1556	- Reading `mirror/cached` through `docker-proxy` after a restore proves the proxy still has it
1557	  in its cache, not that the proxy is unblocked. `mirror/uncached` is what proves the unblock:
1558	  it is served only if the proxy reaches the upstream again.
1559	- While the upstream is cut, the first read of an image that is not cached fails after about
1560	  20 s (the connect timeout of Nexus) and puts the proxy in `AUTO_BLOCKED_UNAVAILABLE`; the
1561	  next reads answer in 0.03 s with `manifest unknown`, which does not mean the image does not
1562	  exist.
1563	
1564	**Measured on the real bench (2026-11-17, datomir).** Source: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-534-measures.md`
1565	(steps 0 and 9).

1567	| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
1568	|---|---|---|
1569	| H-CUTDELAY | **held** | first read of an uncached image with the upstream at zero replicas: 20 s (`502`, connect timeout, proxy `AUTO_BLOCKED_UNAVAILABLE`), then 0.02 to 0.03 s (`manifest unknown`); pods gone 1 to 2 s after the scale |
1570	| H-UNBLOCK | **held** | the `PUT` of the proxy configuration lifts the block (0.8 s); without it Nexus unblocks itself after 21 s (100 s cut) to 79 s (4.5 min cut), growing with the cut. `restore-upstream` serves `mirror/uncached` at once (0.04 s, digest of the data set). `invalidate-cache`: 204 |
1571	| H-STALE | **held** | cached images are served while cut (0.03 s) with the digest of the data set, also after `invalidate-cache` and the refreshing read, and after the upstream storage was replaced (the upstream was empty) |
1572	| H-REPODEL | **held** | `DELETE` of the three repositories: 204 x3; recreated empty at once (no wait seen); the group connector 8082 answers 401 again; the Nexus pod is not restarted |
1573	| H-PVCDEL | **held** | the claim is `NotFound` 0.09 s after the delete; its UID changes on each reset; `kubectl delete --raw` with a wrong UID: `409 Conflict` |

6	## What it is
7	
8	DEVDESK-504 (NX-01): a disposable Nexus Community instance on the k0s cluster
9	of `datomir`, deployed, provisioned over REST and destroyed with one command, so
10	the registry measurements of the NX stories run against a real Nexus. It is a
11	development tool: the `dk` binary does not import it, nothing in `mise run
12	check` or `mise run ci` touches a cluster, and integration tests skip unless
13	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` is set (and always when `CI` is set).
14	
15	Status: the parameters (step 1), the manifest rendering (step 2), the `kubectl`
16	runner, errors and preflight (step 3), the deployment and its wait (step 4), the
17	secrets store and the descriptor (step 5), the REST client and provisioning
18	(step 6), the destruction (step 7), the command with its mise tasks (step 8) and
19	the guarded integration tests with the source guards (step 9) exist. The
20	preflight only reads the cluster; the writes are the two applies of `Deploy`,
21	the REST calls of `Provision` and the namespace delete of `Destroy`.
22	
23	Validated on `datomir` on 2026-11-16 (step 10, see "First real run" below): `up`,
24	a second `up`, the three read-only integration tests and the destructive
25	lifecycle all ran against a real Nexus 3.98.1-01 Community on k0s. One
26	hypothesis was wrong (a proxy whose upstream does not resolve is refused), and
27	`Provision` now copes with it.

53	## Parameters (`params.go`)
54	
55	Precedence: flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable, then default. `FromEnv(base,
56	getenv)` applies the variables onto `base` and returns a new value (the base is

58	an error naming its variable. `Validate()` runs before any call to the cluster
59	and reports every problem at once. Every value that reaches a manifest is
60	checked against a strict pattern, newlines included. The patterns are meant to
61	keep a value from injecting YAML on their own, but the templates still
62	writes every value quoted: the validation is the first guard, not the only one.

92	  `- x`, `@x`, `%x`, `,x`, `:x`), holds no `": "` and does not end with `:`, so it is

262	## Secrets and descriptor (`secrets.go`, `descriptor.go`)
263	
264	**Secrets.** `Secrets{AdminPassword, PendingAdminPassword, PullPassword}` (JSON
265	`adminPassword`, `pendingAdminPassword`, `pullPassword`; the last two are omitted
266	when empty) is kept by a `SecretStore` (`Load`, `Save`, `Remove`), implemented by
267	`NewFileStore(path)`. `PendingAdminPassword` is the new admin password, written
268	before it is sent to Nexus, so an interrupted change loses nothing.
269	
270	- Path: `DefaultSecretsPath(context, namespace, getenv)` is
271	  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench/<context>/<namespace>/secrets.json`, else
272	  `$HOME/.local/state/...` (`USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset); an empty variable
273	  counts as unset, none of them set is an error, and `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`
274	  overrides the whole path. It is outside every repository and shared by all the
275	  worktrees, so a worktree never keeps a stale admin password of its own.
276	- Modes: the file is `0600`, the folders `Save` creates are `0700`. The write is
277	  atomic (`writeFileAtomic`): a temporary file in the same folder, `chmod`, sync,
278	  rename, then a best-effort sync of the folder so the new name survives a power
279	  cut (errors ignored: Windows and some file systems cannot sync a folder); the
280	  temporary file is removed when anything fails, so a failed `Save`
281	  leaves no partial file and a file left by someone else with a wider mode is
282	  replaced, not kept. POSIX modes are not meaningful on Windows (the test skips).
283	- File name: `NewFileStore` refuses a path whose file name is not `secrets.json`
284	  (`Remove` deletes that file, and a mistyped `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` must not point
285	  it at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`).
286	- Mode on read: `Load` refuses a file with a group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`),
287	  outside Windows, with a `BenchError` that never shows the content and says
288	  `chmod 600 <path>`.
289	- Display: `Secrets` has `String`, `GoString` and `LogValue` methods that all give
290	  `Secrets{redacted}`, so no fmt verb (`%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`, `%s`, `%q`) and no slog
291	  handler prints a password (`TestSecretsAreRedactedWhenFormatted`). The JSON of
292	  the file is unaffected.
293	- `Load` returns `(zero, false, nil)` when the file is absent. A file that is not a
294	  valid JSON object is a `BenchError` that names the path and never shows the
295	  content (the underlying error is kept in `Err`, which is not printed).
296	- `Remove` deletes the file, then the namespace folder when it is empty; it
297	  succeeds when there is nothing to remove, and a folder holding anything else
298	  stays.
299	- Git guard: `NewFileStore` refuses an empty path and touches nothing on disk.
300	  It walks up from the file's folder looking for a `.git` entry (directory or
301	  file, so a worktree counts); with none, the path is accepted without asking
302	  git. With one, it runs `git -C <root> check-ignore -q -- <path>`: ignored is
303	  accepted; not ignored, or git unavailable, is a `BenchError` that says to set
304	  `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` outside the repository. The process runs with the caller's
305	  environment minus `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`,
306	  `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`,
307	  `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`,
308	  `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` and
309	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` (`gitEnvironment`), then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<devnull>` and
310	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the verdict is about the repository of the path and
311	  its own ignore rules, not about a repository or a `core.excludesFile` the
312	  caller's variables or configuration point at (a path ignored only by a global
313	  excludes file is therefore refused). That call is the only process
314	  outside `kubectl.go` and `skopeo.go`; it lives in the package variable `gitIgnores`, so it can
315	  be replaced and found by a source guard.
316	
317	**Descriptor.** `BuildDescriptor(p, DeployResult, ProvisionResult, SeedResult)`
318	returns the `Descriptor` of schema 2 (D-D, D-M; schema 1 was NX-01's):
319	`schemaVersion`, `kubeContext`, `namespace`,
320	`image`, `nexusVersion`, `edition`, `eulaAccepted`, `hosts`, `rest`,
321	`dockerConnectors`, `repositories`, `realms`, `accounts`, `registryAccess`,
322	`upstream`, `dataset`, in that order, which is the
323	order of the struct fields. The three sections of schema 2 (DEVDESK-543):
324	
325	- `registryAccess`: `scheme` `http`, `tlsVerify` `false`, `routing` `path` (a
326	  client reaches the Docker repositories by path on the HTTP NodePort, plain
327	  HTTP; true on the real bench since `docker.pathEnabled` is set, H-PATH).
328	- `upstream`: `service` `bench-upstream`, `image` `Params.UpstreamImageRef()`,
329	  `url` `Params.UpstreamURL` (the one `docker-proxy` mirrors), `persistent`
330	  `true`, `exposure` `port-forward` (the upstream has no NodePort; a client
331	  reaches it through `kubectl port-forward`).
332	- `dataset`: one entry per image of the `SeedResult`, in its order and copied
333	  (never shared): `name`, `tag`, `digest`, `location` (`docker-hosted` or
334	  `upstream`), `cachedInProxy` (= `DatasetImage.PullThrough`: Seed pulled it
335	  through `docker-proxy`). It comes from the `SeedResult`, not from `Dataset()`:
336	  an empty result writes `"dataset": []`, never `null`.
337	
338	`ProxyPending` false, the nominal case of NX-02, lists `docker-proxy` and makes
339	it a member of `docker-group`. `hosts` is `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1`
340	then `DeployResult.NodeIP` when it is not empty; the URLs are `http://<host>:<nodePort>`
341	for each host (`RESTBaseURL(host, p)` is the exported REST origin: brackets for
342	IPv6, `%25` for a zone; the deployment, the descriptor and the command of step 8
343	all build it there). `DeployResult{ReachableHosts, NodeIP}` (step 4) and
344	`ProvisionResult{NexusVersion, Edition, EULAAccepted}` (step 6) are defined in
345	`descriptor.go` and reused by those steps. The account `anonymous` always
346	appears; its `enabled` is a `*bool`, so `false` is written when
347	`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS=false`, and the other accounts write no `enabled`.
348	
349	- `WriteDescriptor(path, d)`: JSON indented by two spaces, one final newline, `0644`
350	  file, atomic through the same helper; the bytes depend on `d` alone.
351	- `LoadDescriptor(path)`: a missing file is `ErrNoDescriptor` (wrapped, use
352	  `errors.Is`); invalid JSON or a `schemaVersion` other than 2 (missing counts as 0)
353	  is an error that names the file and never shows its content. A schema 1 file
354	  is a `*BenchError` (kind `Unclassified`) whose `Check` says to run `mise run
355	  nexus-bench:up` to write it again; `status` reports it as `descriptor:
356	  unreadable (...)` and still prints the pod and REST lines.
357	- `DescriptorPath()`: `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` when set and not empty, else
358	  `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json`, found with `runtime.Caller`, so it does
359	  not depend on the working directory (and does not survive `-trimpath`).
360	- Never in the descriptor: a password or any secret, the path of the secrets file,
361	  a timestamp, a pod name, or the word `password` (`TestDescriptorHoldsNoSecret`,
362	  `TestDescriptorFormat`).
363	
364	The golden `testdata/descriptor.example.json` is the descriptor of `Defaults()`
365	with node IP `192.168.1.31`, Nexus `3.98.1-01`, `COMMUNITY`, EULA accepted. It is
366	checked both ways: `WriteDescriptor` must write exactly these bytes
367	(`TestDescriptorGolden`) and `LoadDescriptor` must read back `BuildDescriptor`'s
368	value (`TestLoadDescriptorGoldenMatchesBuild`). After a deliberate change of the
369	schema, regenerate it with
370	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestDescriptorGolden -update` and review the
371	diff by hand (bump `schemaVersion` when a field changes meaning). The golden holds
372	the whole `Dataset()` (`SeedResult{Images: Dataset()}`), with `mirror/cached` as the
373	only image cached in the proxy.

750	## The command and the mise tasks (`cmd/nexus-bench`, `mise.toml`)
751	
752	`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench` is a `package main` of five files:
753	`main.go` (`deps`, `defaultDeps`, `run`), `flags.go` (flags and parameter
754	resolution), `commands.go` (`up`, `provision`, `down`, `seed`, `cut-upstream`, `restore-upstream`, `reset`, `render`), `status.go` and
755	`usage.go` (the help). `main()` only builds a context cancelled by SIGINT and
756	SIGTERM, calls `run(ctx, args, os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())`
757	and exits with its code. `deps` holds every constructor and library call that
758	reaches a cluster (`newRunner`, `newProber`, `clock`, `newStore`, `newInitial`,
759	`preflight`, `deploy`, `provision`, `destroy`) and, since NX-02a (DEVDESK-544),
760	the doors of the seed and the reads of `status` (`newForwarder`, `newCopier`,
761	`ensureUpstream`, `seed`, `readUpstream`, `readImages`); `defaultDeps` wires
762	`NewExecRunner`, `NewProber`, `NewClock`, `NewFileStore`,
763	`NewKubectlInitialPassword`, `RunPreflight`, `Deploy`, `Provision`, `Destroy`,
764	`NewExecPortForwarder`, `NewSkopeoCopier`, `EnsureUpstream`, `Seed`,
765	`ReadUpstream` and `readImagesAnonymously` (NX-02b adds `cutUpstream`, `restoreUpstream`, `reset` and `unblockProxy`, wired to `CutUpstream`, `RestoreUpstream`, `Reset` and `UnblockProxy`) (which calls `ListImagesAnonymously`),
766	and the tests wire fakes, so no test needs kubectl, skopeo or a network.
767	
768	**Tasks.** Ten, in `mise.toml`, none reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or
769	`test-race` (`mise_tasks_test.go` reads the file and checks it, and checks that
770	`kubectl` is declared on each of them, not in the global `[tools]`, so the CI does
771	not install it; kubectl `1.35`, because `datomir` runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is
772	supported within one minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest
773	accepted; `render` contacts no cluster and declares no kubectl, and the test
774	requires its absence there). `nexus-bench:seed` needs `skopeo` too, which is a
775	tool of the host: mise does not install it, the task does not declare it, and its
776	description says so (`TestMiseSeedTaskNamesSkopeoAsAPrerequisiteOfTheHost`).
777	Arguments follow `--`: mise appends them to the command line.
778	
779	| Task | Runs | Acts on the cluster |
780	|---|---|---|
781	| `nexus-bench:up` | `go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up` | yes |
782	| `nexus-bench:provision` | `... provision` | yes (REST and `exec`) |
783	| `nexus-bench:down` | `... down` | yes (deletes the namespace) |
784	| `nexus-bench:seed` | `... seed` | yes (port-forward, REST reads, skopeo pushes); needs skopeo on the host |
785	| `nexus-bench:cut-upstream` | `... cut-upstream` | yes (scales the upstream to zero) |
786	| `nexus-bench:restore-upstream` | `... restore-upstream` | yes (scale, REST writes, port-forward, skopeo reads); needs skopeo on the host |
787	| `nexus-bench:reset` | `... reset` | yes (deletes repositories and the upstream claim, then provisions and seeds); needs skopeo on the host |
788	| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
789	| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |
790	| `nexus-bench:test` | `go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/...` with `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` set by the task's `env` table (portable, no `env` command) | yes; the tests skip when `CI` is set |
791	
792	**Subcommands and flags.** Every subcommand takes the same parameter flags, one
793	per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
794	`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
795	`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
796	`--upstream-image`, `--upstream-image-tag`, `--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`,
797	`--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`, `--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up`
798	and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and `--rest-host`; `seed`, `restore-upstream` and `reset` add `--rest-host`
799	only, and accept a loopback address only (`cut-upstream` has no REST host: it only scales). `seed` provisions nothing, so there is no EULA to accept). Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
800	output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
801	stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
802	`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
803	the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an
804	upstream is given, by flag or variable) are the library's own. `--accept-eula`
805	becomes `yes` (and `--accept-eula=false` `no`, which beats a variable set to
806	`yes`). `Validate` runs before anything else, `render` included.
807	
808	**Exit codes.** `0` success; `1` failure (invalid parameter, kubectl missing, a
809	step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown
810	subcommand, unknown flag, a value of the wrong type, a missing value, an extra
811	argument), with the help on stderr when the subcommand is missing or unknown.
812	`help`, `-h` and `--help` print on stdout and exit `0`. `go run` (so every
813	`mise run nexus-bench:*`) does not propagate the code: it prints `exit status 2`
814	and exits `1`. Code `2` is only visible when the compiled binary is run directly;
815	the general help says so (`TestHelpSaysGoRunDoesNotKeepExitCodeTwo`).
816	
817	**Interruption.** `main()` cancels the run's context on SIGINT or SIGTERM and
818	then hands the signals back to the default behavior (`context.AfterFunc(ctx,
819	stop)`), so a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down. This is not
820	unit-tested: it lives in `main()`, which the tests do not call.
821	
822	**Output.** The progress of the library steps goes to stdout, then one line
823	`nexus-bench: descriptor written to <path>`. Every failure is one line on stderr:
824	a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its
825	`Error()`, and nothing around it or inside it (no wrapper text, no `Err`, no
826	trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things
827	stand; another error prints its message. No output holds a password
828	(`requireClean` of the tests plants markers in the fakes).
829	
830	**`up`.** Resolve the parameters, then the secrets path
831	(`--secrets`/`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else `DefaultSecretsPath`; with no place for
832	it the run stops before any cluster call and says to set
833	`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`), `newRunner`, `newStore` (the git guard), then, when the
834	bench deploys the upstream (`Params.UpstreamIsBench`), `newForwarder` and
835	`newCopier`: everything that can refuse comes before the first write to the
836	cluster, so a host without skopeo stops `up` before it deploys. Then, as D-J says,
837	`Deploy` (which runs `RunPreflight(OpUp)` itself, so the command does not run a
838	second one), `EnsureUpstream`, `Provision` (the proxy is created and joins the
839	group), `Seed`, and the descriptor. **The descriptor is written only after all of
840	them succeeded**, never on a failure at any step, and a descriptor from an earlier
841	run is left as it was. It is built with `BuildDescriptor(p, DeployResult,
842	ProvisionResult, SeedResult)`, the `SeedResult` being what `Seed` returned: the
843	whole data set. With an upstream URL the bench did not deploy (a flag or
844	`NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL`) there is nothing to scale and nothing to push to:
845	`up` builds no door, calls neither `EnsureUpstream` nor `Seed`, prints `seed:
846	skipped, NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL points at ...` on stdout, needs no skopeo, and
847	describes an empty data set (the behavior of NX-01).
848	
849	**`seed`.** `newRunner`, `newStore`, `newForwarder`, `newCopier` (all before the
850	cluster is touched), then the descriptor of the previous run is read, then
851	`RunPreflight(OpSeed)`, `Seed`, and the descriptor again. `Seed` has no data of its
852	own about Nexus: the version, the edition and the EULA consent are carried over
853	from the descriptor of the previous run, and so are its **hosts**
854	(`DeployResult{ReachableHosts: prev.Hosts}`), hence its `rest` and
855	`dockerConnectors` URLs: the preflight of a seed does not read the node, so it
856	has no address to give, and rebuilding the hosts from it would drop the node
857	address `up` found. The file is not trusted for them: they go through the rule of
858	`NEXUS_BENCH_HOSTS` (`ValidateDescriptorHosts`: an IP address or a host name of at
859	most 253 characters) and a bound of 16 hosts, and a bad host stops the seed before
860	any copy with a message that says to run `up` and does not repeat the host. Known
861	limit: a syntactically valid host name passes, whether it is the node or not is not
862	checked. `provision` never reads the hosts of the previous descriptor. Without a readable descriptor of schema 2 (missing, schema 1,
863	not JSON), or with the descriptor of another bench (another namespace or another
864	context), `seed` stops before any copy with a message that says to run `mise run
865	nexus-bench:up`; the file is not touched. As for `up`, the descriptor is written
866	only after a `Seed` that succeeded. `--rest-host` is accepted for a loopback
867	address only (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`): any other host is refused before
868	any dependency is built, with a message that says seed always goes through
869	127.0.0.1 (the images and the credentials never leave the machine from `seed`).
870	There is no `--accept-eula`. `seed` against an upstream URL
871	the bench did not deploy is refused by `Seed` itself (`SeedFailed`); the command
872	does not second-guess it.
873	
874	**Bounds on what Nexus returns (F3, F6).** The names of the components a message
875	prints are quoted (`%q`, an escape sequence shows as text) and at most
876	`maxSeedNamesShown` (5) are shown, the rest summed up as `and K more`
877	(`shownNames`). `listComponents` reads at most `maxListedComponents` (5000)
878	components in all; past it the listing is an error naming the bound and the
879	number of components (`tooManyError`, a `ProvisionFailed` asking for a reset),
880	with no partial result.
881	
882	**Accepted risks (single-user machines).** F4: the port-forward listens on a
883	loopback port, which another local user could take between the choice of the port
884	and the bind; F5: the skopeo authfile of the seed stays on disk if the process is
885	killed with SIGKILL (it is removed on every other exit). Both assume a development
886	machine with one user.
887	
888	**The seed deadline.** `Seed` gets a context that ends after `Params.Timeout`,
889	counted from the start of the seed (not of `up`), so a copy over a port-forward
890	that hangs cannot hang the command and the library does not have to remember it.
891	A seed that outlasts it fails with exit `1`, a `Deadline` message naming the
892	timeout (`--timeout`/`NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`) and no descriptor; the copies already
893	made are kept and a second `seed` copies only what differs. A cancelled run keeps
894	the plain `cancelled` message.
895	
896	**`provision`.** `RunPreflight(OpProvision)`, `Provision`, then the descriptor,
897	built with `DeployResult{NodeIP: <node address of the preflight>}`. It seeds
898	nothing, but the data set is fixed in the code and `provision` touches neither the
899	images nor the upstream, so it keeps the data set, **re-emitted from the code**
900	(`Dataset()`), never copied from the file: the file's data set is compared to the
901	code's, and counts only when it is the same bench (namespace, context and upstream
902	URL unchanged) and it lists exactly that data set. For another bench, or a file
903	that disagrees (another digest, an image added, removed or moved), the data set is empty and stdout says `provision: the descriptor now
904	lists no data set; run mise run nexus-bench:seed` (without the hint when the
905	upstream is not the bench's, since `seed` refuses it). A descriptor that is
906	missing or of schema 1 has no data set to keep: the file is written with an empty
907	one, with no line.
908	
909	**`down`.** `Destroy` (its own `RunPreflight(OpDown)` first). The descriptor is
910	not touched or created.
911	
912	**`status`.** Read-only: `RunPreflight(OpStatus)` (a missing namespace is its
913	`NamespaceMissing` error, exit `1`), one `kubectl get pods -l
914	app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json`, one probe of the REST origin, the state of
915	the upstream, one read of the descriptor and, when it can, two anonymous REST
916	listings. Six lines, each a finding, exit `0`:
917	
918	    bench: namespace nexus-bench, context datomir
919	    pod: running (nexus-xxx, 1/1 ready, 0 restarts)     | not found | pending ...
920	    rest: ready (http://127.0.0.1:30481)                 | not ready (the cause is not shown)
921	    upstream: ready | cut (0 replicas) | starting (...) | missing (...) | not managed by the bench (...) | unknown (...)
922	    descriptor: matches (<path>) | not found (<path>) | unreadable (<cause>) | differs from the current parameters (<path>) + one line per field
923	    dataset: matches (<n> images) | differs (<n> image(s)) | unknown (<why>)
924	
925	`upstream:` is `ReadUpstream` (deployment missing, cut, starting, ready); an
926	upstream URL the bench did not deploy is `not managed by the bench` and nothing is
927	read; a deployment that cannot be read is `unknown`, without the text of the
928	failure. `dataset:` compares the data set the descriptor lists with the listings
929	of `docker-hosted` (the hosted images) and `docker-proxy` (the images cached in the
930	proxy): one difference per image that is missing, has another digest, or is in
931	the listing and not in the data set (so `mirror/uncached` in the proxy counts). `matches (<n> images compared)` counts the images
932	actually compared (the hosted ones and the ones cached in the proxy, not the whole
933	data set).
934	It is `unknown` when it cannot compare: no readable descriptor, a descriptor with
935	no data set (the line sends to `seed` only when the upstream is the bench's),
936	Nexus not answering, anonymous access off (`--anonymous=false`), a
937	listing that fails or gives no digest. The listings come from
938	`ListImagesAnonymously` (`GET /service/rest/v1/components?repository=<repo>`, the
939	`continuationToken` followed, no `Authorization` header at all, on the loopback
940	REST origin). `docker-group` is never listed (a read through it can cache an
941	image, F9), skopeo is never started, no port is forwarded, nothing is written.
942	
943	The descriptor comparison covers context, namespace, image, both NodePorts, the
944	upstream URL, the upstream image (`upstream image: descriptor ..., current ...`)
945	and the anonymous flag; hosts and versions come from the cluster and are left out,
946	and so is the dataset (the parameters know nothing of it; the `dataset:` line
947	covers it). A schema 1 descriptor is `unreadable` with the message of
948	`LoadDescriptor` (run `mise run nexus-bench:up`).
949	It creates no store, builds no `InitialPassword` and sends no credential.
950	
951	**`render`.** Prints `Render(p)` and nothing else; it builds no dependency (the
952	test runs it with an empty `deps`).
953	
954	**Where the credentials go.** `Provision` and `Seed`
955	are given `RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)`, whatever hosts `Deploy` reached, so the
956	admin and `bench-pull` passwords stay on the loopback by default. `--rest-host <host>`
957	(a host name, an IPv4 or IPv6 address, brackets and a zone allowed; no port,
958	scheme, path, credentials or space, refused before any cluster call with exit
959	`1`) sends them to that host instead, and unless it is a loopback address or
960	`localhost` the command prints on stderr a warning that the credentials travel in
961	clear text. The flag moves the REST origin only: the images of the seed always go
962	through `127.0.0.1` (the port-forward and the NodePort path), and the help of
963	`--rest-host` says so (`up`, `provision`, `seed`). `status` and the deployment
964	wait probe without credentials.
965	
966	**Non-default bench.** After writing the descriptor, if the parameters differ
967	from `Defaults()` (any field but the two timeouts, the two paths, the EULA
968	consent and an empty host list), stderr gets `warning: descriptor.json now
969	describes a non-default bench; do not commit it`. The file is written all the
970	same, at `--descriptor`/`NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR`, else the versioned one. A
971	default bench prints nothing on stderr.

973	## Integration tests and source guards (`bench_integration_test.go`, `guard_test.go`, step 9)
974	
975	Read-only state of the run on 2026-11-16: the three read tests pass (8 subtests)
976	and the lifecycle passes (151 s for two downs and three deployments).
977	
978	**Gates.** Every test of `bench_integration_test.go` starts with
979	`requireBench(t)`: it skips unless `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` and `CI` is empty, so
980	`mise run test`, `check`, `ci` and the CI never reach the cluster. The mise task
981	`nexus-bench:test` sets the variable (`env` table). The destructive test needs
982	two more things: `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1` and `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`
983	(the lifecycle provisions Nexus, so the EULA has to be accepted by the operator).
984	None of the tests writes the versioned `descriptor.json`.
985	
986	**The four tests.** The first three need a bench that is up and provisioned
987	(`mise run nexus-bench:up`): they read the versioned descriptor and the secrets
988	file (`openLiveBench`; the REST URL is the descriptor's one on the loopback) and
989	fail with the command to run when either is missing.
990	
991	| Test | Reads | Writes |
992	|---|---|---|
993	| `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed` | `GET /service/rest/v1/status` without credentials (200), then as admin the repository list and, per repository of the descriptor, its type, format, group members or proxy remote URL | nothing |
994	| `TestIntegrationAnonymousAsDescribed` | the anonymous-access setting as admin, and `GET /repositories` without credentials: 200 when the descriptor says anonymous is enabled, 401 when not | nothing |
995	| `TestIntegrationPullAccountIsReadOnly` | `GET /repositories` as `bench-pull` (200) | one control `POST` of a hosted repository `bench-readonly-probe` as `bench-pull`, which has to be refused with **403**. If Nexus accepts it (any 2xx), the test deletes that repository as admin and fails |
996	| `TestIntegrationLifecycle` | admin listings of repositories, roles and users | destructive, see below |
997	
998	`TestIntegrationLifecycle` runs `Deploy` and `Provision` (first up), compares a
999	snapshot of repositories, roles and users, runs up and provision a second time
1000	and requires the same snapshot (idempotence), then `Destroy` and checks that
1001	`get namespace` answers NotFound, `Deploy` on a fresh instance (the pod must hold
1002	an `admin.password` again), and a final `Destroy`. It uses the parameters of
1003	`FromEnv` and the secrets path of the bench (`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else the
1004	default), refuses to start without the EULA, and refuses when `go test` has less
1005	than 45 minutes left (`lifecycleMinTimeout`: three deployments of up to ten
1006	minutes plus the deletions; the default of `go test` is 10 minutes). The
1007	namespace is whatever the parameters say; the preflight already refuses a
1008	namespace this tool did not create.

1010	**Running it.** The task passes `-timeout 60m` for that reason
1011	(`TestMiseBenchTestTaskRunsTheIntegrationTestsGuarded` requires a `-timeout` of
1012	at least 45 minutes):
1013	
1014	    mise run nexus-bench:test                         # the three read tests, lifecycle skipped
1015	    DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1 NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes mise run nexus-bench:test

1018	cleanup: when a step fails halfway, the namespace stays as it is so that the
1019	cause can be diagnosed (`nexus-bench status`, `kubectl logs`). Clean up with

1023	`go/parser`, name file and line, and each detector has a self-test fed with a
1024	faulty and a correct source held in memory. A failure points at code that breaks
1025	the rule, not at a test to relax.

1028	   `NewExecRunner`, `NewExecPortForwarder`, `NewSkopeoCopier`, `DescriptorPath`,

1463	  upstream. The components of `docker-proxy` stayed at `mirror/cached` alone after
1464	  that read, so it does not cache. What a name in the catalog means for NX-03 to
1465	  NX-05 is not "cached"; only the REST components say what the proxy holds.

1467	  traces fill the log); `REGISTRY_LOG_LEVEL` is not set by the manifest.
1468	
1469	## Cut, restore and reset (`upstream.go`, `restore.go`, `reset.go`, `repoapi.go`, DEVDESK-534, NX-02b)
1470	
1471	Three commands, three mise tasks (`nexus-bench:cut-upstream`, `nexus-bench:restore-upstream`,
1472	`nexus-bench:reset`). Each runs a preflight (`OpCut`, `OpRestore`, `OpReset`, see "Errors,
1473	runner and preflight"); `reset` runs its own, as `down` does, the two others get theirs from
1474	the command. None of them can be run on a custom upstream (`NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL`): the
1475	bench scales and empties only the upstream it deploys.
1476	
1477	**`cut-upstream`** (`CutUpstream`). Reads the upstream, scales it to zero replicas when it is
1478	not already cut (one write, never retried), then waits, until `Params.Timeout`, for no pod of
1479	it to be left, a terminating one included (its volume is still mounted). Idempotent. It
1480	touches neither Nexus nor the descriptor and needs no skopeo, no store and no REST host.
1481	Measured: about 2.5 s.
1482	
1483	**`restore-upstream`** (`RestoreUpstream`). Order: the stored credentials are read first (before
1484	any write); `EnsureUpstream` (one replica, wait for ready); `UnblockProxy`; a check, through a
1485	port-forward and with no credential, that each upstream image has the digest of the data set;
1486	a read of each `PullThrough` image through `docker-proxy` as `bench-pull`, digest equal.
1487	It writes no descriptor and copies no image. `UnblockProxy` reads `docker-proxy` (absent is an
1488	error: `up` creates it), sends again the configuration `Provision` writes (`repositorySpecs`,
1489	never one read back from the instance), which lifts the automatic block, then `POST
1490	/v1/repositories/docker-proxy/invalidate-cache`. Measured: 3 to 7 s with the wait for ready.
1491	
1492	**`reset`** (`Reset`). Order: preflight `OpReset`; custom upstream refused; loopback origin
1493	checked; stored credentials, checked by one admin `GET` (a refused password stops everything
1494	before the first deletion); label of the upstream claim checked; `DELETE` of `docker-group`,
1495	`docker-proxy` and `docker-hosted` (a 404 is already done); replacement of the upstream
1496	storage (below); `Provision`; a wait of 30 s at most (`seedListWait`) for `docker-hosted` and
1497	`docker-proxy` to list nothing; `Seed`. The command reads the previous descriptor before
1498	anything and writes it again after a success, with the previous hosts (a reset reads no node);
1499	the file is the same byte for byte. Measured: about 9 to 11 s. `reset` never changes the admin
1500	password (`Provision` gets an `InitialPassword` that never reads the pod) and never rolls or
1501	restarts the Nexus pod; `nexus-data`, the namespace and the passwords are kept.
1502	
1503	**Storage of the upstream** (`recycleUpstreamStorage`). `CutUpstream`; the claim
1504	`bench-upstream-data` is read and its label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench`
1505	checked (D-P: a claim the bench did not create is never deleted); it is deleted with
1506	`kubectl delete --raw /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/persistentvolumeclaims/bench-upstream-data -f -`,
1507	whose body is a `DeleteOptions` with `preconditions.uid` set to the UID just read. `kubectl
1508	delete pvc --wait=false` was not chosen because it has no precondition: a claim replaced since
1509	the read would be deleted. A claim read without a UID is refused. The delete is sent once; the
1510	wait for `NotFound` lasts until `Params.DeleteTimeout`; then the claim alone (document 5 of
1511	`Render`, `renderUpstreamClaim`, never the whole stream, which would roll the Nexus pod) is
1512	applied again and `EnsureUpstream` runs. A claim already gone is not deleted again, and one
1513	still `Terminating` is waited for.
1514	
1515	> **Warning.** Never put `dryRun` in the query of the raw path (`...?dryRun=All`):
1516	> `kubectl delete --raw` does not honor it and the claim is really deleted (seen on the
1517	> bench, DEVDESK-534 step 9). There is no dry run for this call; check with `get pvc`.
1518	
1519	**Half-way.** An error after the first deletion keeps its kind and cause and ends its check
1520	with "the reset stopped half-way: run `mise run nexus-bench:reset` again, it starts over".
1521	What was deleted stays deleted; the reset is idempotent. The one exception is the
1522	repositories that never empty (`errRepositoriesNeverEmpty`): running again would wait for the
1523	same thing, so the check points at the log of the Nexus pod. A cancelled command prints that
1524	the data set may be half deleted.
1525	
1526	**Rights.** `cut`: get `deployments`, list `pods`, patch `deployments/scale`. `restore`: the
1527	list of `seed`. `reset`: that list, plus delete, create and patch `persistentvolumeclaims`;
1528	never `pods/exec`.
1529	
1530	**Loopback guard.** `restore-upstream` and `reset` send the admin credentials in clear text
1531	and go through the port-forwards of this machine, so `--rest-host` must be `127.0.0.1` or
1532	`::1` (`IsLoopbackRESTHost`, the one predicate of the command and the library). `localhost`,
1533	another loopback address (`127.0.0.2`, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`) and any name are refused;
1534	`requireLoopbackBase` also refuses an origin with user information and parses the host, so
1535	`127.0.0.1@evil.example` fails. The port-forward address is checked too
1536	(`checkLoopbackForward`, shared with the seed).
1537	
1538	**Closed lists.** `benchRepositories` (`docker-group`, `docker-proxy`, `docker-hosted`) are the
1539	only repositories `deleteRepository` accepts; `invalidatableRepositories` (`docker-proxy`,
1540	`docker-group`; a hosted repository has no cache) the only ones `invalidateCache` accepts. A
1541	name outside a list is refused before any request, so a name never decides the path the admin
1542	credentials go to.
1543	
1544	**`up` with a cut upstream (D-Q).** `up` reads the upstream before bringing it back; if it was
1545	cut, it calls `UnblockProxy` after `Provision`, so a second `up` leaves the bench nominal. With a
1546	cut upstream and a `--rest-host` that is not loopback, `up` stops before scaling anything (a
1547	refusal later would leave the proxy blocked, since a second `up` finds the upstream ready). If
1548	the unblock itself fails, the error says to run `restore-upstream`.
1549	
1550	**What to know when using it.**
1551	
1552	- After `reset` the Nexus blobs of the deleted repositories are not compacted: `nexus-data`
1553	  grows with each reset. How to get that space back is not measured.
1554	- The admin and `bench-pull` credentials go to the NodePort on the loopback and the images
1555	  through it: this assumes this machine is the node (as before NX-02b; not new).
1556	- Reading `mirror/cached` through `docker-proxy` after a restore proves the proxy still has it
1557	  in its cache, not that the proxy is unblocked. `mirror/uncached` is what proves the unblock:
1558	  it is served only if the proxy reaches the upstream again.
1559	- While the upstream is cut, the first read of an image that is not cached fails after about
1560	  20 s (the connect timeout of Nexus) and puts the proxy in `AUTO_BLOCKED_UNAVAILABLE`; the
1561	  next reads answer in 0.03 s with `manifest unknown`, which does not mean the image does not
1562	  exist.
1563	
1564	**Measured on the real bench (2026-11-17, datomir).** Source: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-534-measures.md`
1565	(steps 0 and 9).
1566	
1567	| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
1568	|---|---|---|
1569	| H-CUTDELAY | **held** | first read of an uncached image with the upstream at zero replicas: 20 s (`502`, connect timeout, proxy `AUTO_BLOCKED_UNAVAILABLE`), then 0.02 to 0.03 s (`manifest unknown`); pods gone 1 to 2 s after the scale |
1570	| H-UNBLOCK | **held** | the `PUT` of the proxy configuration lifts the block (0.8 s); without it Nexus unblocks itself after 21 s (100 s cut) to 79 s (4.5 min cut), growing with the cut. `restore-upstream` serves `mirror/uncached` at once (0.04 s, digest of the data set). `invalidate-cache`: 204 |
1571	| H-STALE | **held** | cached images are served while cut (0.03 s) with the digest of the data set, also after `invalidate-cache` and the refreshing read, and after the upstream storage was replaced (the upstream was empty) |
1572	| H-REPODEL | **held** | `DELETE` of the three repositories: 204 x3; recreated empty at once (no wait seen); the group connector 8082 answers 401 again; the Nexus pod is not restarted |
1573	| H-PVCDEL | **held** | the claim is `NotFound` 0.09 s after the delete; its UID changes on each reset; `kubectl delete --raw` with a wrong UID: `409 Conflict` |
1574	
1575	Timings: `cut-upstream` 2.5 s, `restore-upstream` 3 to 7 s, `reset` 9 to 11 s. The UIDs of the
1576	namespace, the Nexus pod (0 restart) and `nexus-data` did not change across the resets.
1577	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1 mise run nexus-bench:test` (`bench_scenarios_integration_test.go`:
1578	`TestIntegrationUpstreamCutRestore`, `TestIntegrationResetKeepsInstance`) passes in 52 s.
1579	
1580	## Still to come
1581	
1582	The path that uses this lifecycle (NX-03 onward). This file grows with each step.

3	import (
4		"errors"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/oci"
7	)
8	
9	// Verdict is one registry's answer to a search. The zero value is not a
10	// verdict: it means no answer yet, and Classify never returns it.
11	type Verdict int
12	
13	const (
14		// VerdictOK means rows were found.
15		VerdictOK Verdict = iota + 1
16		// VerdictNoResult means the registry answered and nothing matches.
17		VerdictNoResult
18		// VerdictRefused means unsupported or refused.
19		VerdictRefused
20		// VerdictFailed means network, deadline, 5xx, 429 or unreadable body.
21		VerdictFailed
22	)
23	
24	// String is the verdict as shown to the user.
25	func (v Verdict) String() string {
26		switch v {
27		case VerdictOK:
28			return "ok"
29		case VerdictNoResult:
30			return "no result"
31		case VerdictRefused:
32			return "unsupported or refused"
33		case VerdictFailed:
34			return "failed"
35		}
36		return "pending"
37	}
38	
39	// Outcome is a verdict and its marks. Invariant: Partial is set only with ok
40	// or no result (a partial walk that found nothing is still "no result"), never
41	// with refused or failed.
42	type Outcome struct {
43		Verdict Verdict
44		Partial bool
45		Skipped bool
46	}
47	
48	// ErrQueryTooShort: the catalog was not walked, the query is too short.
49	var ErrQueryTooShort = errors.New("query too short to walk a catalog")
50	
51	// ErrPrefixNotInCatalog: no catalog name carries the entry's prefix.
52	var ErrPrefixNotInCatalog = errors.New("no catalog name carries the entry's prefix")
53	
54	// Classify turns a search answer (error, row count, partial flag) into one
55	// Outcome. An error always wins over n and partial. With no error, n == 0
56	// keeps the Partial mark: the verdict is "no result" and Partial is set when
57	// the walk was cut short.
58	func Classify(err error, n int, partial bool) Outcome {
59		switch {
60		case err == nil && n == 0:
61			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictNoResult, Partial: partial}
62		case err == nil:
63			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictOK, Partial: partial}
64		case errors.Is(err, ErrQueryTooShort):
65			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictNoResult, Skipped: true}
66		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupported), errors.Is(err, ErrPrefixNotInCatalog):
67			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictRefused}
68		}
69		var se *oci.StatusError
70		if errors.As(err, &se) && refusedStatus(se) {
71			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictRefused}
72		}
73		return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictFailed}
74	}
75	
76	// refusedStatus tells a refusal from a failure: the registry refusing the
77	// request (401, 403, 404, 405) or the token endpoint refusing the credentials
78	// (401, 403). Any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is a failure.
79	func refusedStatus(se *oci.StatusError) bool {
80		switch se.Code {
81		case 401, 403:
82			return true
83		case 404, 405:
84			return se.Source != oci.SourceToken
85		}
86		return false
87	}

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

1	package imagesearch
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/oci"
7	)
8	
9	// Verdict is one registry's answer to a search. The zero value is not a
10	// verdict: it means no answer yet, and Classify never returns it.
11	type Verdict int
12	
13	const (
14		// VerdictOK means rows were found.
15		VerdictOK Verdict = iota + 1
16		// VerdictNoResult means the registry answered and nothing matches.
17		VerdictNoResult
18		// VerdictRefused means unsupported or refused.
19		VerdictRefused
20		// VerdictFailed means network, deadline, 5xx, 429 or unreadable body.
21		VerdictFailed
22	)
23	
24	// String is the verdict as shown to the user.
25	func (v Verdict) String() string {
26		switch v {
27		case VerdictOK:
28			return "ok"
29		case VerdictNoResult:
30			return "no result"
31		case VerdictRefused:
32			return "unsupported or refused"
33		case VerdictFailed:
34			return "failed"
35		}
36		return "pending"
37	}
38	
39	// Outcome is a verdict and its marks. Invariant: Partial is set only with ok
40	// or no result (a partial walk that found nothing is still "no result"), never
41	// with refused or failed.
42	type Outcome struct {
43		Verdict Verdict
44		Partial bool
45		Skipped bool
46	}
47	
48	// ErrQueryTooShort: the catalog was not walked, the query is too short.
49	var ErrQueryTooShort = errors.New("query too short to walk a catalog")
50	
51	// ErrPrefixNotInCatalog: no catalog name carries the entry's prefix.
52	var ErrPrefixNotInCatalog = errors.New("no catalog name carries the entry's prefix")
53	
54	// Classify turns a search answer (error, row count, partial flag) into one
55	// Outcome. An error always wins over n and partial. With no error, n == 0
56	// keeps the Partial mark: the verdict is "no result" and Partial is set when
57	// the walk was cut short.
58	func Classify(err error, n int, partial bool) Outcome {
59		switch {
60		case err == nil && n == 0:

67			return Outcome{Verdict: VerdictRefused}

70		if errors.As(err, &se) && refusedStatus(se) {

78	// (401, 403). Any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is a failure.
79	func refusedStatus(se *oci.StatusError) bool {

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)

```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**

```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {

    }

```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

H-UNBLOCK confirmed: `restore-upstream` serves the uncached image in 0.04 s; the `PUT` alone lifts the block in 0.77 s, and without it Nexus waits 21 s after 100 s of cut and 79 s after 4.5 min (the interval grows with the cut duration; cap not measured). H-STALE confirmed: after a cut, `mirror/cached` is served with the dataset digest, even after `invalidate-cache` and a refresh read. H-PVCDEL confirmed: the claim is `NotFound` in 0.09 s and the new one binds when the pod starts; a reset takes 8.8 to 11 s. H-REPODEL confirmed: three `DELETE` at 204, the recreated repositories are empty at once, the group's 8082 connector answers `GET /v2/` with 401, and the Nexus pod keeps its UID with 0 restarts. H-INVAL confirmed: `invalidate-cache` answers 204 on a proxy and 400 on a hosted repository. Question Q2 (proxy configuration changed) was not needed: the proxy keeps `autoBlock: true` and the default delays. **Not verified:** (1) whether blobs are compacted when a repository is deleted, so the disk may grow across resets (the cleanup of blobs is not measured); (2) the credentials sent to the loopback NodePort (`127.0.0.1`) are checked only by the stored-password `GET` on the code path, not by a run with an operator's credentials outside the tests. **Rule evolution (to decide, not written here):** the `kubectl delete --raw` dry-run incident may justify a line in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md` (the tech-writer owns both). **Plane:** DEVDESK-534 (NX-02b), with DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a) before it. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-534-plan.md`, `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-534-measures.md`, `internal/nexusbench/` (`restore.go`, `reset.go`, `repoapi.go`), `bench_scenarios_integration_test.go`; D158.**

Decided (user, archived 2026-11-17; plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, drafted there under this number; Q1 to Q4 settled as recommended, except where stated): (1) The client is the host's `skopeo` (1.18.0 when planned; not pinned by mise), run as a process by `skopeo.go` with a cleaned environment and an explicit policy; a missing binary is `SkopeoMissing`. The bench does not measure Nexus with the client that populated it. (2) The images are generated in Go at seed time as OCI layouts in a temporary directory: uncompressed layer tar, sorted entries, zero timestamps, no `created` in the config, so the digests are stable and pinned in a golden file. A `layerGzip` constant switches the layer to gzip, without name or date, if Nexus refuses uncompressed layers (H-LAYER). Nothing is committed as a binary and nothing comes from the network. (3) The upstream is a `registry:3.0.0` Deployment `bench-upstream` in the namespace, with PVC `bench-upstream-data` (kept across a cut, deleted only by `reset`) and a ClusterIP Service `bench-upstream:5000`. The Deployment manifest carries no `replicas`, so `kubectl scale` owns that field and server-side apply never fights it: a cut scales to 0, a restore to 1. The development machine reaches the upstream by `kubectl port-forward` on loopback, for the seed only. No NodePort: a writable registry is not exposed to the LAN. The PVC is read by name, not by label (this corrects a latent NX-01 bug). (4) The hosted repository is seeded through path routing on the HTTP port (`127.0.0.1:<HTTPNodePort>/docker-hosted/...`). Path routing is off by default on Nexus 3.98.1 (`docker.pathEnabled` is null and `/v2/` answers 404 on the HTTP port): `Provision` sets `pathEnabled: true` on `docker-hosted` and `docker-proxy` (lifted on the real bench, 2026-11-17). (5) TLS verification is disabled only for references whose host is `127.0.0.1` or `::1`, and only with a mandatory path. `seed` refuses a `--rest-host` that is not loopback. Credentials go through a temporary authfile (`0600` in a `0700` directory), never in argv. (6) The dataset is fixed in `dataset.go` and described in the descriptor: `api:1.0.0` and `api:1.1.0`, `team/api:1.0.0` and `tools/cli:0.1.0` in hosted; `shared/base:1.0` in hosted and in the upstream, with different content and digests; `mirror/cached:1.0` in the upstream, pulled once through the proxy; `mirror/uncached:1.0` in the upstream, never pulled. Each image carries a `org.devdesk.nexus-bench.source` label. (7) Absence is proven by a sentinel, `errImageAbsent`, returned only on a registry "manifest unknown"; any other failure stays an error, so an unreachable registry is never read as an empty one. (8) An unlisted digest is accepted. (9) Preflight checks the subresources the code uses (`kubectl auth can-i --subresource`: `deployments/scale`, `pods/portforward`), correcting an NX-01 defect that checked `pods/exec`. (10) `up` is extended: deploy Nexus and the upstream, bring the upstream to one ready replica, provision (the proxy is created and joins the group), seed, then write the descriptor, and only after full success. `seed` alone seeds. (11) The descriptor moves to schema 2 (`registryAccess`, `upstream`, `dataset`); `LoadDescriptor` rejects version 1. Rejected: a native Go registry client (it would share the bias of the client being measured); a public image from Docker Hub (network, mutable tags); an unauthenticated NodePort for the upstream (a writable registry on the LAN); `emptyDir` with reseeding (ad hoc content lost at each cut). (13) Nexus 3.98 enables an SSRF protection on a new installation and refuses a proxy whose remote URL host resolves to a private address, a ClusterIP included (HTTP 400 on `proxy.remoteUrl`). Narrower than turning the protection off. Why: one client and one dataset for every later measure, without a cluster-wide exposure, and a cut that the proxy cannot mistake for an empty registry. No separate ADR: the decision is local to the bench and reversible. **Reserves:** lifted on the real bench on 2026-11-17 (see "Observed on the real bench (NX-02a)" in `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`): H-PATH (false by default, fixed by `pathEnabled`), H-PUSH, H-LAYER, H-PROXYHTTP, H-DNS, H-UPRUN, H-SCALE and H-COMPONENTS held; H-SSRF was a surprise (13). H-UNBLOCK, H-STALE, H-CUTDELAY and H-REPODEL belong to NX-02b and are still assumptions. The duplicate `shared/base:1.0` has two digests. `descriptor.json` is versioned at schema 2. **Plane:** DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a), DEVDESK-534 (NX-02b). Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, `internal/nexusbench/`, `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md` (NX-02); D157.**

## 2026-11-17 — DEVDESK-506 (NX-03): `_catalog` measured on the bench (no decision)

Source: `docs/measurements/2026-11-17-nexus-catalog.md` (raw responses in `docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/`). Nexus `3.98.1-01` Community, bench `datomir`. Facts are measured; nothing is decided.

1. **H1 contradicted.** `_catalog` does not prefix names with the member repository (`api`, not `docker-hosted/api`). There is no global `/v2/_catalog` on the HTTP port (404); only the group connector on its own port (30482) answers at the root.
2. **H2 confirmed for the bench account.** The `bench-pull` and anonymous accounts get the same full lists as admin. The filtering case stays untested: no account in the bench is restricted to one repository.
3. **Correction of 2026-08-10 (`docs/backlog.md` §3.18).** The detailed repository endpoint refuses the pull account with 404 "Repository not found" on this version, not 403. Anonymous gets 403. The version of the earlier instance is unknown.
4. **IS-07 contradicted for members addressed by host and path.** Each member answers on its own path catalogue, so one walk per member is needed. On the group connector one walk finds all six names, but names carry no member, and `shared/base` resolves to the first member only.
5. **Side effect on the bench.** A HEAD on a manifest through `docker-proxy` cached `shared/base:1.0` there. `nexus-bench:status` reports `dataset: differs (1 image)`. Reset it before NX-04.

Sections to revisit (none decided):
- **IS-03** criteria 2 and 5 (`repo_prefix`, parade R1): the prefix filter keeps nothing on this version.

Story: `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`, NX-08 (line ~670). Scope decided by the
user: **partial**. Only the NX-03 measures exist (DEVDESK-506, commit `d0b28076`,
`docs/measurements/2026-11-17-nexus-catalog.md`, raw answers in
`docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/`). NX-04 ("Cached only", upstream cut) and NX-05 (routing,
Bearer realm, redirects, pagination) are not done: none of their answers is written here; the
format, the loader, the fake server and the recorder are made so that they add files, not code.

Effort: **M** (PM said S). The replay part alone (criteria 1 to 5, steps 1 to 6) is S; the
recorder (criterion 6, steps 7 and 8) is what makes it M, because it sends the bench
credentials and must carry the same guards as the rest of `internal/nexusbench`.

## Questions bloquantes (to ask the user; the orchestrator relays them)

Q1 and Q2 block steps 5 and 9 only; Q3 blocks step 6; Q4 blocks nothing but the closing.

- **Q1 — the pull account gets 404, not 403, on the detailed group endpoint (contradiction C1).**
  D161 (NX-07) types only 401/403 on `GET /v1/repositories/docker/group/{name}` as a members
  refusal, and recorded the hypothesis "a pull account gets 403, to confirm on the NX-03 bench".
  Measured on 3.98.1-01: `bench-pull` gets **404 `Repository not found`**, anonymous gets 403
  (`rest-repositories-group-docker-group--{pull,anon}.http`). Replayed through `DetectGroup`
  today: the account's 404, then the anonymous retry's 403, end as a **failed discovery**
  (`unreachable`, footer Error, nothing cached, asked again every time), never `denied`.
  So the main case NX-07 was written for (a pull account) does not reach its own outcome.
  - (a) **Recommended**: NX-08 pins the current behaviour on the real answer (test named after
    it, comment pointing at a new story) and a story is opened: "a 404 on the detailed
    endpoint, after the generic endpoint said `group`, is a members refusal" (NX-07b). NX-08's
    out-of-scope says "no new DevDesk behaviour".
  - (b) Change `membersFailure`/`refusedStatus` in NX-08 and flip
    `TestNexusMembersOtherStatusIsNotARefusal` for 404 on that endpoint (adds UI wording,
    cache and MCP consequences: it is NX-07's territory, not a fixture task).
- **Q2 — tests that model a Nexus that does not exist on 3.98.1 (contradiction C3).**
  `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_catalog_share_test.go` (`TestThreeNexusMembersOnOneCatalogWalkItOnce`
  and its siblings) serves one `/v2/_catalog` with prefixed names (`hosted/nginx`,
  `proxy/nginx-x`, `group/nginx-y`) for three members of a Nexus group on one host, and expects
  `ok` for each. NX-03 contradicts both H1 (no prefix) and IS-07 (no shared host catalog: 404 on
  the HTTP port, one unprefixed union on the group connector). The test is right about the
  walk-sharing code; it is wrong as a picture of Nexus. Correcting it means changing the
  behaviour (IS-03/IS-07, "Corrections conditionnelles"), and the journal of 2026-11-17 says
  the H1 decision is the user's.
  - (a) **Recommended**: open one story "reach a Nexus member's catalog by its own path (H1,
    IS-07)" in Backlog, approach left to the user (`/v2/<prefix>/_catalog` or NX-10's REST
    search); NX-08 adds a comment to the contradicted tests naming that story and the fixture
    test that shows the real answer. Criterion 4 is then met ("une story est ouverte").
  - (b) Wait for the user's H1 decision before closing NX-08.
  - (c) Point the comments at NX-10 (DEVDESK-513) only, with no new story (NX-10 is a Could and
    conditional; it does not cover IS-07's walk sharing).
- **Q3 — which descriptor says the bench version, and what a stale fixture does.**
  The brief names `internal/nexusbench/testdata/descriptor.example.json`. That file is the
  golden of `Defaults()`: its `nexusVersion` is a constant of the test
  (`ProvisionResult{NexusVersion: "3.98.1-01"}`), not something read from an instance, so it
  would not move when the bench does. The fixtures themselves cite
  `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` (versioned, written by `up` from the instance's answer).
  - (a) **Recommended**: compare with `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` (`nexusVersion` and
    `edition`), and **fail** `mise run test` with the command to run (`mise run
    nexus-bench:record`). A bench bumped to another Nexus then forces the fixtures to be
    regenerated in the same PR, which is the point of the criterion.
  - (b) Compare with `descriptor.example.json` as the brief says (it will not see a real bump).
  - (c) Compare with `descriptor.json` but only log (`t.Log`) a stale fixture: never red, easy
    to miss.
- **Q4 — how to close a partial story.** Remaining after this plan: `Cached only` and
  `failed` on real answers (NX-04), and realm, redirect, pagination, port/path routing fixtures
  (NX-05); see "Coverage" below.
  - (a) **Recommended**: split. DEVDESK-511 becomes NX-08a (this plan) and is closed by it; a
    new NX-08b (depends on NX-04, NX-05) adds their recordings with no code change expected

  - (b) Keep DEVDESK-511 In Progress until NX-04 and NX-05 land.

## Starting point (read on `main`, `2faf472f`)

| Where | What exists | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/*.http` (82 files) | one exchange per file: `#` header (`scenario`, `nexus: 3.98.1-01 COMMUNITY (...)`, `measured`, `account`, `redacted`), request line + `Host` + `Authorization: Basic <redacted>` (or none), blank line, status line + whitelisted headers, blank line, body (JSON verbatim, `<empty body>`, or `<HTML body omitted: N bytes, <title>...</title>>`). Name `<scenario>--<admin|pull|anon>.http`. LF endings (`.gitattributes`). | Already redacted by NX-03 (no credential, no token, no cookie, header whitelist, `uploaderIp` redacted). Hosts seen: `127.0.0.1` only, plus `bench-upstream.nexus-bench.svc.cluster.local:5000` in `remoteUrl` (the bench's own service, already in the versioned descriptor). Version: **3.98.1-01 COMMUNITY**, measured 2026-11-17. |

| `internal/oci/catalog.go:32` | DevDesk always asks `/v2/_catalog?n=1000` | the NX-03 catalog files were recorded **without** `n`, except `page-group-n1000--admin` |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:376` (`registryAPIURL`) | keeps the path of the entry URL | an entry `http://127.0.0.1:30481/repository/docker-hosted` walks `/repository/docker-hosted/v2/_catalog` (measured 200) |
| `internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_browser.go:389` (`listsCacheOnly`) | `Cached only` is decided from the config, in the UI package | not reachable from `imagesearch`/`registrymgr` tests; needs NX-04 answers anyway |

| `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` vs `testdata/descriptor.example.json` | identical today; only the first comes from an instance | Q3 |

### Contradictions between the measures and the existing tests (criterion 4)

- **C1 (registrymgr)** — see Q1. Not a wrong test: a wrong premise (D161's "403 for a pull
  account"). Resolution: Q1.
- **C2 (imagesearch, fixable here)** — `TestCatalogHTTPPrefix` and the prefix cases of
  `catalog_test.go:99-193` use a Nexus-shaped prefix (`docker-hosted`) with prefixed names,
  which Nexus 3.98.1 never returns. The filter they test is generic (a Harbor project or a
  GitLab group does prefix its names), so the test is kept and its data made neutral
  (`myproject/api`, prefix `myproject`), with a comment stating the measured Nexus fact and
  naming the fixture test. No behaviour change.
- **C3 (ui)** — see Q2.
- **No contradiction**: `TestCatalogHTTPRefusedAndEmpty` "prefix absent" (refused, now shown on a
  real catalog); `TestNexusRefusedMembersWithoutCredentialIsAnAnonymousRefusal` (403 anonymous,
  measured); "the generic endpoint carries no `memberNames`" (measured `"attributes": {}` for all
  three identities, so step 2 of `DetectGroup` is always reached).
- **Facts handed on, not decided here**: (F1) a proxy's `_catalog` lists `mirror/uncached`,
  which it does not hold (it relays the upstream): input for NX-04/NX-09, pinned by a fixture
  test as "the search shows it"; (F2) `cleanMemberAlias` gives both bench members the alias
  `docker` (`docker-hosted`, `docker-proxy`): two group members with the same label. Display
  only, keys are URL + prefix; flagged for the PM, not fixed here.

## Non-functional requirements

- **No bench in `mise run test`/`ci`** (criterion 5): fixtures are embedded files; the fake
  server is `httptest` on loopback; nothing reads `NEXUS_BENCH_*` or the secrets file.
- **No leak** (criterion 1): every fixture passes a leak check in `mise run test`; the recorder
